pages.title: Video Screen
pages.text: $(warn)Requires NarutoLoading.$()$(br2)Want a working TV in Minecraft? Arrange a grid of item frames on a wall, then drag a video file onto them to create a live $(bold)video screen$() that plays right in the world!

pages.title: How to Use
pages.text: $(bold)1.$() Arrange adjacent item frames all facing the same direction — for example, a 4×3 grid on a wall.$(br2)$(bold)2.$() Aim your crosshair at any frame in the group.$(br2)$(bold)3.$() Drag a video file (mp4, mkv, avi, etc.) into the game window and let go.$(br2)$(note)The video file is automatically copied into the NarutoLoading folder so it can be played back.$()

pages.title: What Happens Next
pages.text: Once the video is set up, DragIt works out the screen boundaries and hands everything over to NarutoLoading for playback.$(br2)The video starts playing for all online players immediately — no extra steps needed!

pages.title: Video vs. Image Frames
pages.text: A $(bold)video screen$() is powered by NarutoLoading — the item frame entities become $(bold)invisible$() and the video is drawn directly on the wall surface.$(br2)A regular $(bold)image frame$() (from dropping an image file) keeps the item frame entities visible with a still picture layered on top.
